messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT ALERT — KV_CACHE_MEMORY_GROWTH on hosted-runtime-prod
incident-bot: Severity: P1 | Affected service: hosted-runtime (kv-cache layer) | Symptom: memory climb -> OOMs on several shards | Pager: @emma @dylan

emma: ack. I'm on it. gathering a quick snapshot of affected hosts and traffic.

dylan: oncall runtime here, looking now. any customer reports?

carmen: support seeing a spike in error reports from a few customers using very long prompts — support ticket ids: #3256 #3257. Errors look like 500s and chunked responses.

ben: grabbing logs from the federated kvcache pods in prod-us-east-1. early hint: prefetch depth and continuous-batching combo pushed effective memory per-shard way up.

ben: paste logs:
```
[2026-03-15T20:03:21Z] kvcache: prefetch_enqueue depth=64 session_id=xyz
[2026-03-15T20:03:22Z] batching: continuous_batch size=128 avg_seq_len=4096
[2026-03-15T20:03:22Z] kvcache: mem_used=3.1GB mem_limit=3.2GB shard=rtp-12
[2026-03-15T20:03:23Z] runtime: OOM on shard rtp-12: requested 512MB, available 80MB
[2026-03-15T20:03:23Z] eviction: failed to free enough memory, eviction_queue=high
```

emma: that matches the alert. looks like a regression in the batching/prefetch defaults surfaced in a recent runtime rollout. do we have the rollout id handy?

dylan: yup — rollout 2026-03-15-runtime-v2.4.1 rolled ~19:40 UTC. suspect change: default `prefetch_depth` bumped from 8->48 in canary config. continuous batching thresholds also loosened.

carmen: customers affected are high-L token workloads (code assistants, debug dumps). severity: degraded responses and truncated outputs. some retries are amplifying load.

emma: immediate mitigation plan:
- throttle prefetch depth to safe default (8)
- cap continuous-batch max size to 32
- canary the config change to 5% then 100% when healthy
- route high-length sessions to a lower-prefetch pool as fallback

emma: Dylan — can you push a hotfix config to prod canary? Ben — be ready to roll back pods if needed. I'll update incident ticket and draft customer comms.

dylan: will do. applying canary config now.

dylan: command I'm running:
```
# hotfix: cap prefetch and batch size (canary 5%)
redwoodctl rollout config set --env=prod \
  --selector=runtime=hosted \
  --set runtime.kv.prefetch_depth=8 \
  --set runtime.batch.max_continuous_size=32 \
  --canary 5 \
  --message "hotfix: throttle prefetch + cap batch size to mitigate OOMs"
```

incident-bot: Change accepted. rollout id: RB-20260315-01 (canary 5%). Monitoring for 5m.

ben: can we also enable a temporary per-session token limit for new sessions to reduce amplification while canary runs? quick patchable header enforcement on the edge could help.

emma: yes do that as a temporary safety net. add header cap -> 20k tokens for new sessions.

carmen: drafting customer-facing note (short):
```
We're investigating errors affecting long-prompt sessions in hosted runtime. We have deployed a mitigation that reduces prefetch and batching aggressiveness; you might see lower latency variance and reduced truncations. Follow-up with detailed root cause in 24-48h.
```

dylan: canary looks stable so far (5m): no new OOMs on canary shard group, errors down 78% for canary traffic.

dylan: bumping to 25% canary.

incident-bot: RB-20260315-01 scaled to 25% at 20:10:45Z

ben: monitoring mem across shard fleet — mem pressure dropping, eviction counts down. pushing edge header cap now.

ben: edge header enforcement command:
```
ek-add-rule --env prod --name session-token-cap --match "new_session" --set max_tokens=20000
```

emma: good. while we verify, let's keep rollout incremental. Carmen — send the short note to affected customers and offer a status update channel.

carmen: sent initial comms to the ticket threads and set expectation for follow-up in 6h.

dylan: 25%->100% complete. RB-20260315-01 applied globally at 20:22:10Z. monitoring closely.

incident-bot: RB-20260315-01 complete. No new OOMs for 15m post-rollout. Incident ticket INC-20260315-72 created.

ben: metrics: memory used per-shard back to baseline (~1.1GB avg). continuous batch sizes capped. CPU stable. support error rate down to normal.

emma: thanks team. next steps:
- postmortem to identify how prefetch default change shipped without perf regression test (owner: runtime eng)
- add a perf gate in CI for prefetch/batch combos (owner: runtime infra)
- longer-term: auto-throttle prefetch based on observed shard mem headroom
- customer follow-up in 24h with RCA and ETA for a more robust fix

carmen: noted; I'll draft the customer RCA and coordinate messaging.

dylan: filing a follow-up PR to add a CI regression test for kvcache mem with large prompt synthetic load.

emma: handing off follow-on work to runtime team. I'll close the pager but keep incident ticket open until RCA done. thanks everyone :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Pager closed by emma at 20:44:20Z. Resolution: hotfix config applied (prefetch_depth=8, batch.max_continuous_size=32); edge session cap enabled. Monitoring shows stable memory and error rates. INC-20260315-72 -> status: monitoring -> RCA pending.

carmen: leaving notes for support and marking affected customers for follow-up.

ben: I'll keep an eye on the infra dashboards for 6h and post if anything anomalous shows up.

emma: ok wrapping up. if anything new pops up, reopen this thread or page @dylan directly. good job team. :tada:
